data.name: VR火灾逃生应急演练(VR fire emergency simulation system)
data.detailed_description:
VR Fire Escape Emergency Exercise System is a fire emergency simulation program produced by Hong Xing (Beijing) Technology Co., Ltd. It aims to make the experience masters the fire escape skills and understand through the immersive simulation operation Correct emergency measures to reduce their own injury.

The program built-in Chinese version and English version, you can switch within the program.

The VR hardware device used for the development and testing of this program is HTC VIVE. The operation status of VR hardware devices from other brands is unknown. Please be aware.

reviews.review:
VR火灾逃生应急演练 is a very different kind of VR experience from the games I normally play. It is built around emergency fire evacuation training rather than entertainment, with the main purpose being to let me practise what I should do during a fire through a simulated environment. I actually think that is a useful idea for VR because being placed inside a virtual emergency situation can make the experience feel much more immediate than simply reading instructions.

The main focus is learning how to react during a fire and understanding the correct emergency measures. I am placed into the simulation and have to interact with the situation rather than just watching a video about fire safety. I like that approach because it gives the experience an actual purpose. It is not trying to turn fire into a shooting game or make the situation unnecessarily exciting. The whole point is to make me think about escaping safely and responding properly.

The VR presentation is naturally the strongest part for me. The program was developed and tested using HTC Vive and supports SteamVR with standing and room scale play. Being able to look around the environment and interact using tracked controllers makes the training feel more hands on. There is also both Chinese and English language support, which is useful because I can switch between the two versions inside the program.

At the same time, I do not think this is something I would play repeatedly like a normal game. There are no traditional progression systems, combat mechanics or large amount of content to keep me entertained for hours. Once I understand what the simulation is trying to teach me, there is not much reason to keep coming back unless I specifically want to practise the emergency procedure again. I think that is completely fine for a training program, but it does limit how I can judge it as a game.

The biggest issue for me is the age and technical state of the program. It originally released in December 2017, and the developer later acknowledged that the application can have problems such as black screens and flashing with newer VR hardware. The developer also stated in 2025 that the program no longer receives technical support and would be changed into a free application mainly for communication purposes. That makes the experience difficult to recommend as a polished modern VR title, even though the original idea is still useful.

I also think the presentation feels more like an educational simulation than a finished commercial game, which is exactly what it was designed to be. The environments and interactions are there to support the training rather than provide entertainment. Because of that, I found myself judging it more on whether the concept works than on whether it has impressive graphics or deep gameplay. I think it does succeed at showing how VR can be used for practical emergency training, even if the actual software feels dated now.

Overall, VR火灾逃生应急演练 is an interesting educational VR program that has a worthwhile purpose but has clearly aged. I like the idea of using an immersive simulation to practise fire evacuation and emergency responses, and I think the VR format makes sense for this type of training. The lack of traditional game content is not really a problem considering what it was made for, but the technical issues and lack of ongoing support are much harder to overlook. I think it is worth experiencing as a small example of VR being used for practical training, but I would not treat it as a full game in the normal sense.

Rating: 6.6/10
